wave: SEMANTIC PRESERVATION / CENSUS BLINDNESS -- CFG silently treats a let-else diverge block as non-diverging straight-line code
wave_title: Following this session's syntax-coverage sweep (which confirmed let-else diverge blocks ARE correctly walked by CONCURRENCY/PERSISTENCE/STATE via the shared StatementWalker trait), checked whether CFG -- the most semantically load-bearing walker, since it computes real successor edges rather than just finding sites -- handles the same construct. It does not: lower_stmts dispatches purely via stmt_expr, which returns None for every syn::Stmt::Local, so a let-else statement (diverge block included) is silently skipped with `continue`. Empirically confirmed: a function whose only conditional early exit is a let-else diverge block (`let Some(v) = x else { return 0; }; v`) is reported as exactly one block with a single unconditional Return successor -- indistinguishable from a function with no conditional exit at all.

generation_model.gap_discovered_by: Direct adversarial testing: after establishing that let-else/if-let/raw-address-of are correctly walked by the StatementWalker-sharing trio (concurrency/persistence/state), checked CFG specifically since it has its own independent statement-dispatch logic (lower_stmts, not StatementWalker) and is the one walker whose job is computing real successor edges, not just finding evidence sites. Grepped cfg.rs for diverge/Expr::Let/RawAddr handling, found none, then wrote a probe test to empirically confirm the resulting successor graph is wrong (reports unconditional Return) rather than assuming from the missing match arm alone.

priority_classification: semantic preservation / census blindness (priority 3-4) -- CFG's own contract (core::semantic::control_flow) states successor edges are computed wherever 'source syntax structurally determines them'; a let-else diverge block's control-flow effect IS structurally determined by syntax alone (no type/name resolution needed), so this is squarely inside CFG's own stated scope, not a case where the gap is justified by the same type-resolution wall that excuses CALL/EFFECT's other gaps. This makes it a real, currently-unrepresented mandatory case within CFG's declared closure, not an out-of-scope one.

design_decisions.question: Implement the full CFG-splitting fix now (branch the block into a success edge and a lowered diverge-block successor, mirroring the existing if/match/loop pattern), or document the gap honestly and defer?
design_decisions.decision: Document and defer, with a falsifiable regression-baseline test rather than a silent gap. A full fix requires extending lower_stmts's core branch-splitting logic (the same machinery backing if/match/loop, which has extensive existing test coverage this session has not exhaustively re-validated) to a new statement shape, with new edge cases (nested let-else, let-else inside a loop body, a diverge block that itself contains further control flow) not yet explored. Given CFG is the single most safety-critical walker in this extractor (its output is real successor-edge truth, not merely an evidence candidate), the risk of an under-validated change introducing a WORSE bug (an incorrect successor claimed as EpistemicStatus::Observed) outweighs the value of closing this specific gap in one pass with the remaining session budget. This matches the exact precedent this repository has already established for R4.3.7 and R4.6's own statement-level-only boundary: an explicitly acknowledged, falsifiable gap is preferred over a rushed, under-verified fix to safety-critical logic.
